Chapter 1. Installation

Source: vignettes/articles/01-Installation.Rmd
01-Installation.Rmd

Decant is an R package. It needs R 4.1 or later and four packages that come with every R installation: Matrix, methods, stats and utils.

1.1 Install Decant 

install.packages("remotes")
remotes::install_github("kroy3/Decant")
  • install.packages("remotes") installs the helper package that can install packages from GitHub. Skip it if you already have remotes.
  • remotes::install_github("kroy3/Decant") downloads Decant from its GitHub repository, builds it and installs it into your R library.

1.2 Optional packages

Some features need additional packages. Decant works without them and tells you when one is missing.

Package Needed for Install with
SeuratObject (5.0 or later) RunDecant(), DecantDE() install.packages("Seurat")
edgeR, limma ambient_de(), DecantDE() BiocManager::install(c("edgeR", "limma")) 
install.packages("Seurat")
install.packages("BiocManager")
BiocManager::install(c("edgeR", "limma"))
  • The first line installs Seurat, which also installs SeuratObject.
  • BiocManager is the installer for Bioconductor packages.
  • The last line installs edgeR and limma, which the differential expression functions use for normalisation and testing.

1.3 Check the installation 

library(Decant)
packageVersion("Decant")
#> [1] '0.4.0'
  • library(Decant) loads the package. No message is printed when it loads successfully.
  • packageVersion("Decant") prints the installed version. Include it when you report a problem.

1.4 What you need from your experiment

Decant measures the ambient RNA from empty droplets, so it needs the raw (unfiltered) count matrix, not only the filtered one. For 10x Genomics data this is the raw_feature_bc_matrix folder written by Cell Ranger, next to filtered_feature_bc_matrix. If you only kept the filtered matrix, you can still use Decant with an approximate soup (see Chapter 11.6), but the result is less reliable.
